fields.text: Ancient Silver Dragon Silver dragons are among the most chivalrous of all dragonkind; they wield frost and cold as weapons, can walk on clouds, and dwell high upon snowy mountain peaks or deep in steep, misty valleys. Although they typically make their lairs among the highlands, the pursuit of justice leads silver dragons to travel far and wide—often into the very heart of realms overrun by evil. These exemplars of righteousness are ceaseless in their determination to help the weak, spread honor, and stamp out evil. Silver dragons are sleek and sinuous. Their hides resemble nothing so much as a suit of gleaming armor, lending further credence to the popular myth that silver dragons are the paladins of dragonkind. The zeal with which they seek out, confront, and defeat evil is unsurpassed even among their metallic cousins, and they adhere to strict codes of honor usually passed down from parent to hatchling. On occasion, they instead learn these codes from trusted mentors, usually other silver dragons or gold dragons. As they age, they become even more dedicated to their codes, often adding new and even more restrictive clauses to the systems that guide their behavior. Silver dragons are incredibly altruistic and regularly consort with the citizens of goodly societies, of which they consider themselves protectors and guides. In addition to responding to evil threats, silver dragons work to prevent evil from taking root in the first place, and they ensure mortals under their care are well fed, educated, and treated with dignity. Although silver dragons can seem overzealous or even eager to join the fight against evil, they know that the best way to rid the world of corruption is to stamp out strife and disillusionment at their source, not to passively sit back and watch it grow into an unsolvable problem. Silver dragons can be vindictive, but they can also be forgiving; for evildoers who seek to atone for their sins and turn over a new leaf, the support of a silver dragon is both unwavering and invaluable. Many silver dragons are also drawn to religious endeavors, venerating deities such as Iomedae, Sarenrae, and other deities concerned with justice, virtue, and redemption. **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)): DC 44 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 42 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 [Ancient Skaveling](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2151) **Source** [Pathfinder #184: The Ghouls Hunger](/Sources.aspx?ID=147) pg. 63 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), echolocation 60 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +29, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +4 **Int** +3 **Wis** +8 **Cha** +4 **Echolocation** The ancient skaveling can use its hearing as a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense at the listed range. --- **AC** 37 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +27 **Will** +29 **HP** 270 --- **Speed** 15 feet, fly 30 feet **Melee** fangs +29 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d12+16 piercing plus ghoul fever and paralysis **Melee** wing +29 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d8+16 bludgeoning plus paralysis **Bone-Shattering Screech** ([Auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16), [Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [Fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) The ancient skaveling unleashes a devastating screech that not only chills the bones but shatters them. The screech can be heard throughout the region and alerts all creatures in the Hanging Castle. Creatures in a 20-foot emanation take 12d6 sonic damage and must attempt a DC 36 Will save. The ancient skaveling can't use Bone-Shattering Screech again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Bone-Shattering Screech for 24 hours.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is frightened 2
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, is frightened 3, and is [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). **Ghoul Fever** ([disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46)) **Saving Throw** DC 36 Fortitude; **Stage 1** carrier with no ill effect (1 day); **Stage 2** 2d6 negative damage and regains half as many Hit Points from all healing (1 day); **Stage 3** as stage 2 (1 day); **Stage 4** 2d6 negative damage and gains no benefit from healing (1 day); **Stage 5** as stage 4 (1 day); **Stage 6** dead, and rises as a [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=52) the next midnight **Paralysis** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [Necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) Any creature hit by the skaveling's Strikes must attempt a DC 36 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35).
**Failure** The creature is [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28). It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each save.

Sky dragons live above the clouds near the summits of mountains. They maintain a strong religious tradition, a unique practice among imperial dragons that sets them apart as much as their wings do. Desperate souls risk steep cliffs and loose snow to seek these dragons' counsel, and most sky dragons gladly help those who make the journey, but they expel any express hostilities or badger without hesitation. The sky dragon's wings aren't true wings, but long fins fused to their forearms; their scales also form only very slowly. Young dragons coil tightly in their lairs as they absorb minerals that color and harden their scales. Even adults often wrap around pillars out of habit. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Ancient Sky Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1130) **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 80 **Perception** +32; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Auran](/Languages.aspx?ID=15), [Celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), [Infernal](/Languages.aspx?ID=19), [Sylvan](/Languages.aspx?ID=10) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +28, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +35, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +28, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +32, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +34, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +28, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +28 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Mist Vision** Fog and mist don't impair a sky dragon's vision; they ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from fog and mist. --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +31 **Ref** +28 **Will** +32 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 335 **Immunities** electricity, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Countered by Fire** If the sky dragon takes fire damage, the elemental magic of metal within them is tempered. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and AC, and their jaws Strikes don't deal electricity damage. This limitation ends if the dragon uses Breath Weapon.
**Fed by Earth** ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) When a sky dragon is targeted by an [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55) spell or effect, they leave a cloud of pulverized dust and gravel that swirls in the eddies of the dragon's flight. For 1 minute, the dragon is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) while flying.
**[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) 90 feet, DC 38 --- **Speed** 60 feet, fly 160 feet **Melee** jaws +36 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+16 piercing plus 1d12 electricity **Melee** claw +36 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+16 slashing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) **Melee** tail +36 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103), [reach 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+16 bludgeoning plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) **Divine Innate Spells** DC 42 - **1st** [Feather Fall](/Spells.aspx?ID=111), [Gust of Wind](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) - **4th** [Gaseous Form](/Spells.aspx?ID=129), [Invisibility](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) **Breath Weapon** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65)) The dragon shoots a ball of electricity that deals 9d12 electricity damage and 2d12 sonic damage in a 30-foot burst within 60 feet (DC 40 basic Reflex save). They can't use Breath Weapon again for 1d4 rounds. See divine lightning below. **Coiling Frenzy** The dragon makes one claw Strike and one tail Strike in either order, each against the same target. If either Strike hits, the dragon automatically [Grabs](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=18) the target. **Divine Lightning** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) A good sky dragon who worships a deity channels divine power through its attacks, making them more effective against [fiends](/Traits.aspx?ID=70) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). Any electricity damage it deals becomes good damage against fiends or positive damage against undead. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Breath Weapon whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **[Greater Constrict](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=19)** 3d10+11 bludgeoning, DC 40 **Perfected Flight** A sky dragon can hover in place without spending an action, and they automatically succeed at all [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks to [Maneuver in Flight](/Actions.aspx?ID=30). **Stunning Electricity** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [Evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93)) The dragon rapidly coils, then unleashes crackling lightning that deals 5d12 electricity damage in a 60-foot emanation. They maintain a strong religious tradition, a unique practice among imperial dragons that sets them apart as much as their wings do. Desperate souls risk steep cliffs and loose snow to seek these dragons' counsel, and most sky dragons gladly help those who make the journey, but they expel any express hostilities or badger without hesitation. Young dragons coil tightly in their lairs as they absorb minerals that color and harden their scales. Even adults often wrap around pillars out of habit. When the imperial dragons first arrived in [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26), each was well-attuned to the elemental planes they hailed from. As the war between the [Elemental Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=8) raged on and the benevolent lords fell one by one, the [Planes of Metal](/Planes.aspx?ID=24) and [Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) sealed themselves away. For the dragons who originated from the Corroded Core, their very existence was now at stake. These dragons flew from mountaintop to mountaintop, seeking refuge from the then-perilous Tian Xia overrun by warring yaoguai. Finally, upon the mountain peaks of Chenlun, Gossamer, Kelsang, Kimu, Kullan, Kyojin, and the Wall of Heaven, celestial beings answered the dragons' cries for help. What the dragons no longer had in elemental [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505), these celestials provided through divine blessings and essence. With their nature changed, the dragons as a species survived. In time, their proximity to the sky and the deities they serve became their namesake. The most well-known of imperial dragons due to their deep involvement with mortals, the sovereign dragons' name comes from their mandate of selecting rulers—but at some point, the dragons themselves joined the list of worthy candidates. Other imperial dragons suspect the sovereign dragons offered their connection to the elemental cycle to attain forbidden magic, evidenced by their lack of any vulnerability to wood or ability to feed on fire, despite being creatures of the earth. Most hesitate to question the sovereigns' authority. While some appreciate their impartial nature, others fault this adherence to neutrality. Regardless, the sovereign dragons' charm and centuries of experience in subtle manipulation have made them exceptional negotiators. Almost all sovereign dragons appear gold in color. Their hair ranges from common colors found among humans to bright reds, greens, or blues. They're the only dragons with five digits per claw, a mark of special importance. fields.text: Ancient Sovereign Dragon The most well-known of imperial dragons due to their deep involvement with mortals, the sovereign dragons' name comes from their mandate of selecting rulers—but at some point, the dragons themselves joined the list of worthy candidates. Other imperial dragons suspect the sovereign dragons offered their connection to the elemental cycle to attain forbidden magic, evidenced by their lack of any vulnerability to wood or ability to feed on fire, despite being creatures of the earth. Most hesitate to question the sovereigns' authority. While some appreciate their impartial nature, others fault this adherence to neutrality. Regardless, the sovereign dragons' charm and centuries of experience in subtle manipulation have made them exceptional negotiators. Almost all sovereign dragons appear gold in color. Their hair ranges from common colors found among humans to bright reds, greens, or blues. They're the only dragons with five digits per claw, a mark of special importance. Other imperial dragons dismiss this claim to status and instead tease the sovereign dragons over their need to wear armor, even while in their draconic forms. There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Heralds of—and heralded by—the primal forces of thunder and lightning, stormcrown dragons meld the majesty of fierce storms and mighty dragons. Driven by emotion and curiosity, these mercurial dragons can change from friend to foe or threatening to thoughtful in mere moments. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Ancient Stormcrown Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4180) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 172 **Perception** +30; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), motionsense (precise) 120 feet, [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +38, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +31, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +31, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +31, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +35, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +31, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +27 **Str** +6 **Dex** +9 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +4 Motionsense A stormcrown dragon can detect the movement of nearby creatures through vibration and air movement.This precise sense works only against creatures and objects that moved in the previous round. --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +33 **Ref** +33 **Will** +30 +2 status to all saves vs. [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) **HP** 360 **Immunities** [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 20 **Weaknesses** [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=585) 20 **[Frightful Presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=64)** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 100 feet, DC 37
**Superconductor** **Trigger** The dragon is targeted by an attack or spell; **Effect** The dragon uses the displaced air or magical trajectory of the attack as a channel for its electrical energy. The dragon attempts a storm bolt Strike against the attacker, regardless of range. --- **Speed** 60 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** jaws +35 ([Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+16 piercing **Melee** claw +35 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+16 slashing **Melee** tail +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=765)), **Damage** 2d10+16 bludgeoning plus 3d6 sonic **Melee** antler +28 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d6+16 piercing plus 2d12 electricity **Ranged** storm bolt +35 ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [range increment 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 3d12+10 electricity **Primal Innate Spells** DC 40 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Gale Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1994) - **3rd** [Wall of Wind](/Spells.aspx?ID=1753) (at will) - **6th** [Cursed Metamorphosis](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479) (at will) - **8th** [Punishing Winds](/Spells.aspx?ID=1643) **Command Lightning** ([Concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Requirements** The dragon's last action was to use Draconic Frenzy or [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527) or [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) trait and they're in an area of stormy weather; **Effect** The dragon directs a bolt of lightning at a creature within 100 feet, dealing 4d12 electricity damage with a DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save **Coronal Cloak** When the dragon spends an action to Hover while in stormy weather, they become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) until they [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) or until the beginning of their next turn, whichever comes first. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges Galvanic Barrage whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Galvanic Barrage** ([Electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) The dragon exhales a massive bolt of lightning at one creature within 100 feet, dealing 10d12 electricity damage with a DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. The lightning then arcs to a creature of the dragon's choice within 60 feet of the previous target with the same effect. The dragon can't target the same creature more than once, and they must have [line of effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=2382) to all targets. The bolt can continue to arc this way until the dragon runs out of targets or until a target critically succeeds at their save. The dragon can't use Galvanic Barrage again for 1d4 rounds. **Smooth Flying** The stormcrown dragon doesn't fall if they don't [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) during their turn, and they're unaffected by [strong winds](/Rules.aspx?ID=2821) or similar effects unless they choose to be. **Storm Howl** Whenever a creature critically fails a save against one of the stormcrown dragon's abilities that deals electricity damage, that creature is also permanently [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66).

Time dragons are implacable enemies of the sinister [hounds of Tindalos](/Monsters.aspx?ID=702), also denizens of the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=46). Although hounds of Tindalos also seek to prevent any tampering with the flow of time, time dragons relentlessly hunt down every hound they encounter, despite the apparent common ground between them. No dragon has told the reason for this enmity to outsiders, but scholars speculate that time dragons and hounds of Tindalos might have different, competing opinions for what the proper flow of time should look like. Occasionally, those stalked by the hounds are rescued by time dragons who appear from nowhere to slay their pursuers, although this isn't necessarily a lucky break if the intervening dragon also objects to their activities. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 42 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 37 [Ancient Time Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4184) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 176 **Perception** +33; (36 initiative) [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=164), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=158), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +32, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +38, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +38, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +34, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +35 **Str** +9 **Dex** +6 **Con** +10 **Int** +7 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 44 **Fort** +38 **Ref** +32 **Will** +35 **HP** 470 **Immunities** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) **Immortal** Time dragons age, but don't die from old age.
**Starflight** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) A time dragon can survive in outer space and fly at incredible speed, taking 3d20 hours to reach a destination within the same solar system or 3d20 days for destinations beyond. They can carry up to six passengers of at least one size category smaller than themself, protecting them from the void of space.
**Decelerating Dodge** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** The dragon is targeted with a ranged Strike or spell attack; **Effect** The dragon slows time to evade, gaining [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 60 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** jaws +38 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d10+19 piercing **Melee** claw +38 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d8+19 slashing **Melee** tail +36 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 25 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d12+19 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 42 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Daze](/Spells.aspx?ID=1482), [Time Sense](/Spells.aspx?ID=2611) - **3rd** [Behold the Weave](/Spells.aspx?ID=2601), [Time Pocket](/Spells.aspx?ID=2610) - **4th** [Morass of Ages](/Spells.aspx?ID=2603) - **5th** [Quicken Time](/Spells.aspx?ID=2604), [Stagnate Time](/Spells.aspx?ID=2605) - **6th** [Awaken Entropy](/Spells.aspx?ID=2600) - **7th** [Behold the Weave](/Spells.aspx?ID=2601), [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) (at will; Dimension of Time and Universe only) - **8th** [Quandary](/Spells.aspx?ID=1644) - **9th** [Foresight](/Spells.aspx?ID=1537) - **Constant (9th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** When the dragon scores a critical hit with a Strike, they recharge their Timeshift Breath. **Second Chance** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per round; **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet (including the time dragon) fails a saving throw or skill check; **Effect** The target rerolls the check, but must use the second result. The target is then temporarily immune to Second Chance for 24 hours. **Temporal Eddies** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The dragon [Strides](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) up to their Speed, leaving behind afterimages of their past and future selves in each space they move through. Until the end of the dragon's next turn, they can use any of these spaces as the origin of their Strikes, spells, and other abilities. Observers also perceive the dragon in all these spaces simultaneously and must succeed at a DC 15 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to target the dragon or fail to affect it. A creature can take a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) action to attempt to identify the dragon's true location with a successful DC 40 Will save. **Timeshift Breath** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) The dragon breathes a blast of temporal energy, warping time in a 80-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386). Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 42 Will save. The dragon can't use Timeshift Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is slowed 2 for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature shifts briefly forward in time, vanishing and reappearing at the beginning of the time dragon's next turn in the same location (or an adjacent space if their former location is occupied), unaware that any time has passed. While timeshifted, time pauses for that creature, and it cannot take actions or be affected by anything else.

Stories across Golarion warn children about the monsters that dwell in the shadows, but no story captures the reality of the umbral dragon. Natives of [the Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36), these occult dragons are at home in the darkness, using it to their advantage both in and out of battle. Umbral dragons rarely worry about fighting fairly, emerging from hiding to strike unwary foes and using their magical breath without compunction. Similarly, in social situations, they often remain in the shadows, operating through other creatures. Even in direct conversation, they frequently obscure their true intent, preferring to avoid ever being pinned down with a solid answer. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 42 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 37 [Ancient Umbral Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4188) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 181 **Perception** +33; [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), voidsense (precise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [D'ziriak](/Languages.aspx?ID=58), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=162), [Shadowtongue](/Languages.aspx?ID=166) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +34, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +38, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +34, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +37, [Netherworld Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +34, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +38 **Str** +10 **Dex** +6 **Con** +7 **Int** +5 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +5 **Hide in Shadows** The dragon can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) in [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) even if they don't have [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372).
**Voidsense** The dragon can taste animating void energy, allowing them to sense creatures with [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83) as a precise sense. It can also sense [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) creatures with void healing, like [shadows](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=469), when they are inside solid objects. --- **AC** 44 **Fort** +34 **Ref** +31 **Will** +34 +2 to all saves vs. [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693) **HP** 375 **Immunities** [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) Umbral Pall ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) 90 feet. Shadows surround the dragon. The radius of all light from light sources and the areas of light spells in the aura are halved.
**Pin Shadow** ([shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) **Trigger** A creature within reach of the dragon's claw uses a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action or leaves a square during a move action it's using; **Requirements** The triggering creature is in [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) or [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) and has a shadow; **Effect** The dragon makes a claw Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, the trigger creature also has its shadow pinned in place, restricting its movement. The creature treats the area of the dragon's aura as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2586) until it uses an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to unpin its shadow. If the area was already difficult terrain, the creature treats it as greater difficult terrain. --- **Speed** 60 feet, fly 200 feet **Melee** jaws +38 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)), **Damage** 4d8+18 piercing plus 2d8 void **Melee** claw +38 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d6+18 slashing **Melee** tail +36 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 25 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d10+18 bludgeoning **Occult Innate Spells** DC 39 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485), [Read Aura](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646) - **9th** [Darkness](/Spells.aspx?ID=1480) (at will), [Umbral Journey](/Spells.aspx?ID=1729) **Rituals** DC 42 - **2nd** [Create Undead](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) (shadows only) - **4th** [Shadow Double](/Rituals.aspx?ID=154) **Devour Undead** The dragon's jaws Strikes have the benefit of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) property rune and deal an additional 7d6 force damage to undead. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges its Tenebrous Breath whenever it scores a critical hit with a Strike. **Drain Vigor** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) When the dragon deals void damage to a living creature with its jaws Strike, the umbral dragon gains 20 [temporary HP](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last for 1 minute and the creature must succeed at a DC 40 Fortitude save or become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 (drained 2 on a critical failure). Further damage dealt by the dragon's jaws Strike increases the drained condition value by 1 on a failed save (2 on a critical failure), to a maximum of drained 4. **Tenebrous Breath** The umbral dragon exhales in one of two ways. They can't use Tenebrous Breath again for 1d4 rounds.
  • **Darkness** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The dragon breathes a blast of darkness that deals 21d6 void damage in a 50-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures take force damage instead of void damage.
  • **Shadows** ([occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) The dragon breathes a blast of shadows in a 50-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must attempt a DC 42 Fortitude save.
    **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
    **Success** The creature is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 3 for 1 round.
    **Failure** The creature is enfeebled 3 for 1 minute.
    **Critical Failure** The creature is enfeebled 3 for 1 minute and [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round.

While the other primal dragons hail from the Elemental Planes, the cruel and unceasingly malicious umbral dragons originate in the depths of the Shadow Plane. Their sleek black scales and serpentine grace allow them to strike from hiding, and they are known for playing with their prey before finally finishing it. These creatures of shadowy energy and unwholesome appetites prefer the necrotic flesh of undead creatures to any other meal. This strange hunger can be of accidental benefit to nearby humanoid societies, but ultimately they hunt and kill undead creatures for the taste, rather than out of any desire to protect others from the undead. The benefit is always short-lived, however. When umbral dragons exhaust their preferred prey, they turn on whatever living creatures happen to be nearby. Umbral dragons sometimes go to great lengths to obtain their favorite meals, even creating undead creatures that they then feast upon. For all their power, umbral dragons are uninterested in fair battles. When faced with foes that pose any kind of actual danger to them, umbral dragons flee into the shadows and seek to strike back through pawns or minions rather than risk their own lives. Their treasure hoards are varied and diverse, often augmented by loot stolen from crypts the dragons have turned into feeding grounds. Underworld dragons embody the pressure between tectonic plates, the heat behind geysers, and flash fires that ignite when the conditions are just right. Natural alchemists, they innately understand reagents and catalysts. While some research the effects of magic on material reactions, the majority of underworld dragons concentrate on building their hoards. They scour the world for carved gemstones and artifacts of precious minerals, both of which they see as distilled essence of earth's bounty. Underworld dragons appear angular and sharp; their scales glow as if superheated from within, and their hair flickers like tongues of flames. An intense fire glows behind their gazes, suggesting they could ignite items with a mere thought, and their breath ripples the air as a testament to the heat contained within their bodies. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Ancient Underworld Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1136) **Source** [Bestiary 3](/Sources.aspx?ID=66) pg. 85 **Perception** +28; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) (imprecise) 60 feet, smoke vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Ignan](/Languages.aspx?ID=18), [Terran](/Languages.aspx?ID=22), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +23, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +25, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +32, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +29, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +27, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +29, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +24, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +25, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +3 **Con** +6 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +5 **Smoke Vision** Smoke doesn't impair an underworld dragon's vision; they ignore the [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) condition from smoke. --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +25 **Will** +28 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 295 **Immunities** fire, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145) **Countered by Water** If the underworld dragon takes damage from a spell with the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait, the elemental magic of fire within them is momentarily dampened. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, their jaws Strikes don't deal fire damage, and also lose their sweltering heat aura. This limitation ends if the dragon uses Breath Weapon.
**Fed by Wood** When an underworld dragon is struck by a weapon made primarily of wood or affected by a spell with the [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) trait, the dragon's internal fiery essences are stoked with the added fuel. Their breath weapon recharges, and the fire damage from the dragon's jaws increases by one die until the end of the dragon's next turn.

Creature Family Dragon, Underworld Source Bestiary 3 pg. 83 Underworld dragons embody the pressure between tectonic plates, the heat behind geysers, and flash fires that ignite when the conditions are just right. Natural alchemists, they innately understand reagents and catalysts. While some research the effects of magic on material reactions, the majority of underworld dragons concentrate on building their hoards. They scour the world for carved gemstones and artifacts of precious minerals, both of which they see as distilled essence of earth's bounty. Underworld dragons appear angular and sharp; their scales glow as if superheated from within, and their hair flickers like tongues of flames. An intense fire glows behind their gazes, suggesting they could ignite items with a mere thought, and their breath ripples the air as a testament to the heat contained within their bodies. Underworld dragons make their homes close to fault lines, active or dormant volcanoes, and regions with natural seismic activities. Locations with hot springs and fume holes are particularly popular, as they provide many alchemical and magical ingredients. Aside from vaults stuffed with treasure, underworld dragon lairs are also laboratories, dedicated to uncovering secrets in cultivation, elements, magic, and any other mysteries of interest. Vizier dragons are primarily concerned with the education and cultivation of people. People fascinate vizier dragons in all their riotous, contradictory complexity. Why do some people excel, and others falter and fail? Why does one person become a saint and the next a tyrant? Why do some become legends in their own time, while others labor in ignominy? **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 42 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 40 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 37 [Ancient Vizier Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4196) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 188 **Perception** +36; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 80 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=157), [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=158), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Gnomish](/Languages.aspx?ID=159), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=162); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +29, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +31, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +38, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +38, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) +36, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +36, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +35 **Str** +9 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +7 --- **AC** 44 **Fort** +35 **Ref** +33 **Will** +39 +1 status to all saves vs. [magic](/Skills.aspx?ID=27) **HP** 450 **Immunities** dragontongue, [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696), [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) **Dragontongue** When a dragon speaks, the universe listens. Vorpal dragons are most notorious for their keen [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) magic. Even the least of these dragons can sever a foe's head in a single lucky stroke. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite creature: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. Some might even wear their favorite severed heads as a macabre necklace. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Ancient Vorpal Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4200) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 192 **Perception** +33; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 120 feet **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=164), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156), [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=119), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +31, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +35, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +29, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +31, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +31 **Str** +9 **Dex** +5 **Con** +6 **Int** +6 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +5 --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +36 **Ref** +30 **Will** +33 +2 status to all saves vs. [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) **HP** 330 **Immunities** [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), decapitation, [paralysis](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), sleep **Resistances** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) 20, physical 15 (except adamantine bludgeoning) **Cutting Rebuke** **Trigger** A creature within reach of the dragon's chin blade that the dragon can see makes a Strike against the dragon; **Effect** The dragon makes a chin blade Strike against the triggering creature. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 180 feet **Melee** chin blade +35 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d8+17 slashing plus vorpal binding **Melee** claw +35 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d6+17 slashing **Melee** tail +33 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 25 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=708)), **Damage** 3d12+17 slashing **Ranged** pinion +31 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [propulsive range increment 120 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=677), [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=724)), **Damage** 3d8+13 slashing **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 40 - **6th** [Seal Fate](/Spells.aspx?ID=2024) (×3) - **7th** [Interplanar Teleport](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) (First World and the Universe only) - **8th** [Beheading Buzz Saw](/Spells.aspx?ID=1365), [Field of Razors](/Spells.aspx?ID=1370) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Feast of Blood whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Feast of Blood** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) The dragon inhales sharply, pulling blood from wounds and into the dragon's maw. Each creature in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes their current [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) plus 14d6 void damage (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save). The dragon gains [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) equal to half the greatest amount of void damage dealt to a single creature this way. The dragon can't use Feast of Blood again for 1d4 rounds. **Heads Will Roll!** **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** The vorpal dragon swoops across the battlefield, sweeping their axe-bladed tail through their foes. The dragon [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) twice; at any point during this movement, the dragon makes up to two chin blade Strikes, each against a different creature within reach. The dragon's multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until all Strikes are made. **Vorpal Binding** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) The vorpal dragon beheads its foes— sometimes without killing them. A vorpal dragon's chin blade Strikes count as having the [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2853) weapon property rune for the purpose of [weaknesses](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893). Whenever the vorpal dragon critically succeeds on a chin blade Strike, it deals an additional 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), which can be ended normally.
When a vorpal dragon rolls a natural 20 on a chin blade Strike, the target must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save; this has the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait. On a failure, the creature is beheaded. A creature beheaded this way does not automatically die; instead, their head and body live on, disconnected but mystically linked, with the head controlling the body from afar. A beheaded creature is [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 2 and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) as they attempt to coordinate movements from an unusual perspective, or clumsy 4 and [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) and [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) if their head can't perceive their body from its location. These conditions are suppressed if the body holds its head, and don't apply to actions performed exclusively by the head, mind, or voice. If the body is killed, the head can live on, but destroying the head kills the body as well. This effect can be ended only by [_regenerate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1648), [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1456), or any effect that restores life to the dead; only effects that restore an incomplete corpse will replace an absent or destroyed body, however. The dragon can choose to instantly kill a creature when beheading them, as per the vorpal weapon property rune's activation. **Gruesome Cuts** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) [Persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) inflicted by the dragon, even magically, carries a poison that inhibits clotting. Healing the creature to full HP doesn't end the bleeding, the DC of any flat check to recover is 2 higher, and the DC to stop the bleeding using [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) is 40. This poison can be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) (DC 40), and successfully doing so ends the bleeding.

_Nethys Note: This creature was printed with 33 HP._ Canny, patient, and creative, wailing dragons are adepts of sound and psychology. With both their physiology and innate connection to arcane magic allowing them to produce and shape sound waves, these reclusive creatures are heard much more often than seen. Named for their tendency to use uncanny keening vocalizations to communicate across long distances and startle prey, wailing dragons haunt locations that create interesting or useful echoes, such as canyons or caverns. Though ruthless predators when needed, most wailing dragons devote their energy toward investigating the effects sound has on the environment and the bodies and minds of creatures. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Ancient Wailing Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4204) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 196 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), echolocation (precise) 120 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +27, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +30, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +25, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +27, [Music Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +25, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +25, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) +33, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +27 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +4 **Int** +2 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +6 **Echolocation** A wailing dragon can use its hearing as a precise sense at the listed range. --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +29 **Will** +24 +2 status to all saves vs. [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) and [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) **HP** 33 **Immunities** [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Resistances** [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) 20 Subsonic Drone ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) 120 feet, A creature who enters or begins their turn in the area must attempt a DC 33 Fortitude save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's subsonic drone for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1.
**Failure** The creature is sickened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is sickened 3.
**Destructive Interference** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541)) **Trigger** A foe within 90 feet uses an [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) effect; **Effect** The young wailing dragon releases a burst of noise, attempting to drown out the triggering sound. It makes a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) check against the effect (counteract rank 8, counteract modifier +28). --- **Speed** 45 feet, fly 110 feet **Melee** jaws +28 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d10+16 piercing **Melee** claw +28 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d6+16 slashing **Melee** tail +26 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 25 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d12+16 bludgeoning **Ranged** shriek +26 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [range 90 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=765)), **Damage** 3d6+8 sonic **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 34 - **Cantrips (8th)** [Figment](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528) - **8th** [Noise Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616) (at will), [Shatter](/Spells.aspx?ID=1670) **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges their Resounding Roar whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Eerie Call** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Requirements** The dragon is [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96); **Effect** The dragon's wail draws in unsuspecting opponents. Anyone that can hear the Eerie Call must attempt a DC 36 Will save or become [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) by the sound. A fascinated creature must spend at least 1 action [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) the dragon each turn, and the dragon can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this affect for up to 1 minute. **Natural Mimic** The dragon can imitate any sound or voice that it has heard. This has the effect of 2nd-rank [_ventriloquism_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1740) (DC 36) but is a nonmagical effect. **Resounding Roar** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=765)) The dragon unleashes a thunderous call that deals 16d6 sonic damage in a 60-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). The dragon gains a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. Any creature that is adjacent to the dragon at any point during its movement takes 8d6 sonic damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On a critical failure, the creature is also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1 hour. A creature can be affected only once per Reverberating Rush.

fields.text: Ancient Wailing Dragon Nethys Note: This creature was printed with 33 HP. Canny, patient, and creative, wailing dragons are adepts of sound and psychology. With both their physiology and innate connection to arcane magic allowing them to produce and shape sound waves, these reclusive creatures are heard much more often than seen. Named for their tendency to use uncanny keening vocalizations to communicate across long distances and startle prey, wailing dragons haunt locations that create interesting or useful echoes, such as canyons or caverns. Though ruthless predators when needed, most wailing dragons devote their energy toward investigating the effects sound has on the environment and the bodies and minds of creatures. Recall Knowledge - Dragon (Arcana): DC 36 Unspecific Lore : DC 34 Specific Lore : DC 31 Creature 15 Ancient Wailing Dragon Uncommon Gargantuan Arcane Dragon Source Draconic Codex pg. 196 Perception +29; darkvision, echolocation (precise) 120 feet Languages Common, Draconic Skills Acrobatics +27, Athletics +30, Crafting +25, Intimidation +27, Music Lore +25, Nature +25, Performance +33, Stealth +27 Str +8 Dex +6 Con +4 Int +2 Wis +4 Cha +6 Echolocation A wailing dragon can use its hearing as a precise sense at the listed range. AC 36 Fort +26 Ref +29 Will +24 +2 status to all saves vs. auditory and sonic HP 33 Immunities deafened, paralyzed, sleep Resistances sonic 20 Subsonic Drone (aura, auditory) 120 feet, A creature who enters or begins their turn in the area must attempt a DC 33 Fortitude save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's subsonic drone for 1 minute. Critical Success The creature is unaffected. Success The creature is sickened 1. Failure The creature is sickened 2. Critical Failure The creature is sickened 3. Destructive Interference Reaction (arcane, auditory) Trigger A foe within 90 feet uses an auditory or sonic effect; Effect The young wailing dragon releases a burst of noise, attempting to drown out the triggering sound. It makes a counteract check against the effect (counteract rank 8, counteract modifier +28). Speed 45 feet, fly 110 feet Melee Single Action jaws +28 (Magical, reach 20 feet), Damage 3d10+16 piercing Melee Single Action claw +28 (Agile, magical, reach 15 feet), Damage 3d6+16 slashing Melee Single Action tail +26 (Magical, reach 25 feet), Damage 3d12+16 bludgeoning Ranged Single Action shriek +26 (Magical, range 90 feet, sonic), Damage 3d6+8 sonic Arcane Innate Spells DC 34 - Cantrips (8th) Figment - 8th Noise Blast (at will), Shatter Draconic Frenzy Two Actions The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. Draconic Momentum The dragon recharges their Resounding Roar whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. Eerie Call Two Actions (Arcane, auditory, emotion, fear, mental) Requirements The dragon is hidden or undetected; Effect The dragon's wail draws in unsuspecting opponents. Anyone that can hear the Eerie Call must attempt a DC 36 Will save or become fascinated by the sound. A fascinated creature must spend at least 1 action Seeking the dragon each turn, and the dragon can Sustain this affect for up to 1 minute. Natural Mimic The dragon can imitate any sound or voice that it has heard. This has the effect of 2nd-rank ventriloquism (DC 36) but is a nonmagical effect. Resounding Roar Two Actions (Arcane, sonic) The dragon unleashes a thunderous call that deals 16d6 sonic damage in a 60-foot cone (DC 36 basic Fortitude save). On a critical failure, a creature is also deafened for 1 minute. The dragon can't use Resounding Roar again for 1d4 rounds.In addition, if the area overlaps with an area of magical silence or includes a creature affected by magical silence, the roar attempts to counteract the silence effect (counteract rank 8, counteract modifier +28). Reverberating Rush Three Actions (Arcane, sonic) The dragon Flies three times. The dragon gains a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. Any creature that is adjacent to the dragon at any point during its movement takes 8d6 sonic damage (DC 33 basic Fortitude save). On a critical failure, the creature is also deafened for 1 hour. A creature can be affected only once per Reverberating Rush. Creature Family Dragon, Wailing Source Draconic Codex pg. 195 Canny, patient, and creative, wailing dragons are adepts of sound and psychology. With both their physiology and innate connection to arcane magic allowing them to produce and shape sound waves, these reclusive creatures are heard much more often than seen. Named for their tendency to use uncanny keening vocalizations to communicate across long distances and startle prey, wailing dragons haunt locations that create interesting or useful echoes, such as canyons or caverns. Though ruthless predators when needed, most wailing dragons devote their energy toward investigating the effects sound has on the environment and the bodies and minds of creatures. Whisper dragons are keen collectors of rumors and secrets who spend centuries honing their information networks and relationships. They generally do so not out of an intent to hold the information over others or to use for their own machinations, but simply because the process of learning and gathering information is fulfilling. Their hoards are sparse compared to those of other dragons, as they hold their true treasures—secrets—in their minds. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Ancient Whisper Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4368) **Source** [Monster Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=276) pg. 135 **Perception** +28; The target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 and can't reduce their frightened condition for 1 minute or until the dragon reveals the secret. As a reaction when the affected creature attempts a check, the dragon can reveal their secret to discomfit them, requiring them to roll twice and take the lower result; this is a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect.

You can apply the following adjustments to whisper dragons of any age. Some whisper dragons bind an informant’s secrets into contracts, obtaining their information in exchange for granting them a boon. To make a dragon with this ability, replace Steal Knowledge with the following. Draft Contract Three Actions (occult, manipulate) The dragon produces a contract for a single living mortal. This contract can grant a single boon or ability, the extent of which is dependent on the power of the dragon, in exchange for one piece of knowledge the mortal possesses. The mortal must willingly sign their true name to the contract, as well as the knowledge they wish to surrender. Upon signing, the mortal forgets the bartered information, which cannot be restored by any means short of a wish ritual; if they restore this knowledge, they lose the boon granted by the contract. A whisper dragon can develop strong bonds with their informants that allow them to view the world through their informants’ senses. To make a dragon with this ability, replace Information Network with the following ability. When they do, they lose all sensory information from their own body. The dragon can Sustain this effect for up to 1 hour and Dismiss it as a free action. A whisper dragon might take on a humanoid guise to gather information without attracting notice. To make a dragon with this ability, give them the following ability. Change Shape Single Action (concentrate, occult, polymorph) The dragon takes on the appearance of a Small or Medium humanoid. Their humanoid shape has a specific, persistent appearance. In humanoid shape, the dragon loses their jaws, claws, and tail Strikes, but retains their attack bonuses with any weapons they wield. Their Speed is reduced to 25 feet. Naizraa The whisper dragon Naizraa resides in a sumptuous palace high on the bluffs of northern Qadira’s Saray Coast. She keeps a close eye on the intrigues of Qadira’s nobility and sometimes offers her patronage to talented individuals seeking information or influence, in exchange for a secret of their own. The most feral and least intelligent of all the chromatic dragons, white dragons are brutish, predatory, and chiefly motivated by self-preservation. Nearly all other dragons look down on white dragons as hopelessly hotheaded and dull, though this does not make them any less dangerous—in fact, it may mean the opposite. It’s nearly impossible to treat with white dragons, not because they lack the capacity to do so, but because they just don’t care to. They are as difficult to deal with as they are quick to anger, and they become incensed at almost anything. When a white dragon does speak, it spews threats, inane jokes, and incoherent babbling as a prelude to attacking—and when the attack comes, it’s bloody and relentless. Thankfully, white dragons prefer very cold, remote locations that are far from people. Dwelling on glacial mountaintops or in ice caverns beneath forbidding tundra, they treat the lands around them as their own personal hunting grounds. They fly out to feed or terrorize other creatures, especially those who trespass near the dragon’s territory, then bring any treasure back to be displayed in icy niches in their lairs. They collect all kinds of valuables, with a slight preference for items with high utility—such as tools, trade goods, and fine food—over coins or jewels. The ability to shape ice lets white dragons rearrange their lairs exactly to their specifications, and they take great pride in how they’ve decorated their homes over the years. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Ancient White Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=141) **Source** [Bestiary](/Sources.aspx?ID=2) pg. 115 **Perception** +30; darkvision, scent (imprecise) 60 feet, snow vision **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=2), [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) +24, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) +23, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) +31, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +28, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) +26 **Str** +8 **Dex** +3 **Con** +7 **Int** +2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +3 **Snow Vision** Snow doesn’t impair a white dragon’s vision; it ignores concealment from snowfall. --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +30 **Ref** +26 **Will** +24 +1 status to all saves vs. magic **HP** 330 **Immunities** cold, paralyzed, sleep **Weaknesses** fire 15 **Blizzard** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27)); 50 feet. After the dragon uses its Breath Weapon, a fierce blizzard of blinding snow surrounds its body for 1 round. Everything in the aura is diffcult terrain for other creatures that are on the ground, climbing, or flying. The blowing snow also makes all creatures in the area concealed. While the blizzard rages, the dragon’s dragon chill extends to the full area of the blizzard.

fields.text: Ancient White Dragon The most feral and least intelligent of all the chromatic dragons, white dragons are brutish, predatory, and chiefly motivated by self-preservation. Nearly all other dragons look down on white dragons as hopelessly hotheaded and dull, though this does not make them any less dangerous—in fact, it may mean the opposite. It’s nearly impossible to treat with white dragons, not because they lack the capacity to do so, but because they just don’t care to. They are as difficult to deal with as they are quick to anger, and they become incensed at almost anything. When a white dragon does speak, it spews threats, inane jokes, and incoherent babbling as a prelude to attacking—and when the attack comes, it’s bloody and relentless. Thankfully, white dragons prefer very cold, remote locations that are far from people. Dwelling on glacial mountaintops or in ice caverns beneath forbidding tundra, they treat the lands around them as their own personal hunting grounds. They fly out to feed or terrorize other creatures, especially those who trespass near the dragon’s territory, then bring any treasure back to be displayed in icy niches in their lairs. They collect all kinds of valuables, with a slight preference for items with high utility—such as tools, trade goods, and fine food—over coins or jewels. The ability to shape ice lets white dragons rearrange their lairs exactly to their specifications, and they take great pride in how they’ve decorated their homes over the years. What is a wish? A wish dragon would call it the truest expression of self—each individual wish reveals something of deep importance to the wisher, and no two wishes are ever quite the same. Whether the wish is one of creation or destruction, justice or vengeance, love or hate, wish dragons seek to understand what makes it important to the wisher and view their ability to make it a reality as a gift that helps them make sense of the world. **[Recall Knowledge - Dragon](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35)): DC 41 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 39 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 36 [Ancient Wish Dragon](/Monsters.aspx?ID=4208) **Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 200 **Perception** +32; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) (imprecise) 60 feet **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Draconic](/Languages.aspx?ID=156) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +32, [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +33, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +32, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +33, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +34, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +31, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +40, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +35 **Str** +6 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +9 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 --- **AC** 42 **Fort** +31 **Ref** +31 **Will** +35 +2 status to all saves vs. arcane **HP** 360 **Immunities** [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=696) **Best Wishes** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) 30 feet. Being near a wish dragon gives other creatures a greater sense of what they truly wish for, bolstering their sense of purpose while also distracting them from the task at hand. Creatures in the aura take a –1 status penalty to Perception but gain a +2 status bonus to Will saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. The wish dragon can't gain the benefit of their own aura or other actions that use the aura, and they can choose to exclude any creatures from any benefit of the aura or action that uses the aura.
**Wished Away** **Trigger** The dragon is critically hit by an attack; **Effect** The dragon wishes not to be hurt by this attack, gaining [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 25 to all damage against the triggering attack. --- **Speed** 50 feet, climb 50 feet, fly 200 feet **Melee** jaws +36 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d8+16 piercing **Melee** claw +36 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d6+16 slashing **Melee** tail +34 ([Magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [reach 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 4d10+16 bludgeoning **Arcane Innate Spells** DC 41 - **Cantrips (9th)** [Message](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598) - **9th** [Cozy Cabin](/Spells.aspx?ID=1474), [Creation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1477) (at will), [Energy Aegis](/Spells.aspx?ID=1512), [Safe Passage](/Spells.aspx?ID=1659), [Sure Strike](/Spells.aspx?ID=1709) - **Constant (5th)** [Truespeech](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Breath of Loss** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) The dragon breathes a warm, gentle breeze of mist that creates the feeling of when deepest desires are achieved. As the breeze dissipates, the feeling of loss overwhelms creatures' senses, dealing 19d6 mental damage in a 50-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 41 Will save). A creature that critically fails its save is also consumed with the memory of the moment and is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 2. The wish dragon can't use Breath of Loss again for 1d4 rounds. **Destructive Wish** **Requirements** An illusion from Wish Come True is currently active; **Effect** The wish dragon [Dismisses](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the illusion of Wish Come True, which shatters into magical fragments, dealing 9d6 force damage with a DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save to all creatures in a 50-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of the illusion. **Draconic Frenzy** The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order. **Draconic Momentum** The dragon recharges Breath of Loss whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike. **Grant Wish** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per month; **Effect** The wish dragon instantly grants the benefits of a critical success with the [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual to a mortal creature. This has no cost. That creature specifies what they wish for, but the interpretation is up to the wish dragon. A summoned wish dragon can't use this ability. **Wish Come True** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The dragon creates an illusion in an unoccupied square within 60 feet that appears to all other creatures that can see it to be the manifestation of their deepest material desire. This has the effects of [_illusory object_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1569) (though the illusion might appear to be a creature to certain people) that last for 10 minutes. The wish dragon can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the illusion. Each non-wish dragon creature who begins their turn within 200 feet in [line of sight](/Rules.aspx?ID=2383) of the illusion must attempt a DC 41 Will save. If any creature within reach of the illusion [Interacts](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to touch it, the illusion ends and that creature is invigorated, gaining 2d8 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last for 1 minute.
**Critical Success** The creature disbelieves the illusion and becomes temporarily immune to Wish Come True for 1 hour.
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature is stupefied 2 for 1 round. **Wish You Would** ([Arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Requirements** An [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) from Wish Come True is active; **Effect** The dragon targets one creature within 200 feet currently [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) by Wish Come True, making them believe that the object of their desires is under attack from all those around them and the dragon is the only one they can trust. The target must succeed at a DC 40 Will Save or they become [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) by the dragon for 1 minute. The target may attempt a new save at the end of each of their turns. If the illusion from Wish Come True dissipates, their controlled state immediately ends.
